newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty fears imminent execution of Iranian lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty fears imminent execution of Iranian lawyer.

text.p: Amnesty International said it feared that an Iranian lawyer reported to have been arrested in Iran in 1993 may be at risk of imminent execution.
"Amnesty International fears that Mohammad Assadi may be at risk of imminent execution," the London-based human rights group said in a statement sent to Reuters on Thursday.
The organisation said Assadi was reportedly arrested in September 1993 and held in secret detention in a military prison for a year.
"In March 1997 it was reported that he had been sentenced to death and to confiscation of his property. He is said to be currently held in Evin Prison in Tehran," the statement said.
Amnesty said the charges against Assadi, 68, were unknown to the organisation.

It said reports suggest the reason for his arrest may have been related to his having defended an army officer accused of involvement in an attempted coup in 1980 "whom he had met during an earlier detention."

The statement added: "Other possible charges are reported to be an alleged trip to Israel before the establishment of the Islamic Republic of Iran in 1979, alleged membership of the Freemasons, and alleged purchases of American agricultural material before 1979."
Amnesty said Assadi had been arrested on five previous occasions since 1979.
